season.evidence: Stored Jul-Sep, best mid-July to September; peak-wide ascents Jun 7, Jul 26, Aug 31, Sep 22, Oct 15; searches found no source naming a window, logs cluster July and September, Harts Pass road and snow are the limits.

track.why: Only one route is stored on Dot Mountain. The Jul 13 2025 track starts at Slate Pass (39 m from our pin), passes the Whistler cutoff junction (25 m), skirts the Lago-Carru area and Point 8165, reaches our Dot summit pin within 94 m and returns to the same trailhead; the line follows the stored description.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Oct 6 2023, summited, complete from Slate Pass (5 m); a week past the window and older; also line only loosely at Dot (324 m on the sparse shape). Second choice.
Aug 31 2025 four-day multi-peak trip (Osceola, Carru, Lago, Ptarmigan, Dot ...); complete mechanically but not a clean single-route line.
Sep 1 2024 logged NE ridge from Ptarmigan Peak, starts at the Dot Lake basin, not our Slate Pass line.
Aug 2008 report only, no track; ridge traverse from a Shellrock Pass camp.
Aug 2014 report matches our route description, but no track harvested.

facts.text: In late August a party left the Eureka Creek trail near 5,950 ft and climbed open, lightly wooded slopes (partly on a faint climbers path) toward the Carru-Lago area, dropping packs near 7,300 ft.
Late August: the north side of the Carru-Lago col and the talus below Lago needed almost no snow travel, and the small glacier under Lago has mostly melted away, leaving loose rock.
From the 7,400 ft tarn camp, the early-morning ridge to Dot (west-side ramp around Point 8165) is quick; the register at the top is only a small canister with few entries.
In early September the south approach to Dot was straightforward scrambling with perhaps a class 3 move near the end, and Ptarmigan Peak lies a short stroll along the northeast ridge.
In late August Lago was judged the loosest, rottenest peak of the cluster; test every block on its slopes.

notes: Single route on the peak. Slate Pass trailhead agrees with every Slate Pass track (5-82 m), so no pin move. The 2023-10-06 Dot track (2335602) is 74 miles by its own stats, likely a multi-peak trip.
